# Lanka Global Access - Visa & Immigration Website

A professional website for Lanka Global Access Consultancy, providing visa and immigration consulting services.

## Features

- **Modern Landing Page** - Hero slideshow, services, destinations, and contact info
- **Contact Form** - Formspree integration for client inquiries
- **Responsive Design** - Works on all devices
- **Animations** - GSAP and AOS scroll animations
- **WhatsApp Integration** - Floating chat button

## File Structure

```
visa-website/
├── index.html              # Main homepage
├── contact.html            # Contact form page
├── style.css               # Global styles
├── main.js                 # Main JavaScript
├── README.md               # This file
├── CNAME                   # Custom domain (www.lgavisa.com)
├── robots.txt              # SEO robots file
├── sitemap.xml             # XML sitemap
├── sitemap.html            # HTML sitemap
└── images/                 # Website images and assets
```

## Deployment

This site is deployed on **GitHub Pages** at [www.lgavisa.com](https://www.lgavisa.com).

```bash
# Push changes to deploy
git add .
git commit -m "Update site"
git push origin main
```

## Tech Stack

- HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
- Tailwind CSS (CDN)
- GSAP + ScrollTrigger (animations)
- AOS (Animate On Scroll)
- Font Awesome (icons)
- Formspree (contact form)

## Contact

- **Email**: admin@lgavisa.com
- **Phone**: +94 726338989

**Lanka Global Access** — a static marketing website for a Sri Lankan visa & immigration consultancy, live at **www.lgavisa.com** via GitHub Pages.

- **CDN libraries**: Tailwind CSS, GSAP (+ ScrollTrigger/ScrollTo/TextPlugin), AOS, Font Awesome
- **Formspree** for the contact form backend

| `index.html` (1,268 lines) | Landing page: hero, about, services, stats counters, countries, contact, WhatsApp float button |
| `contact.html` (646 lines) | Contact form → Formspree (`formspree.io/f/mnnzjgle`) |
| `main.js` (456 lines) | `LankaGlobalAccess` class: GSAP animations, scroll effects, mobile menu, counters, parallax, smooth scrolling, loading screen |
| `style.css` (675 lines) | Global styles/animations |
| `sitemap.html/.xml`, `robots.txt`, `CNAME` | SEO + GitHub Pages custom domain |

- Legacy assets present (`glyphicons`, old portfolio/team image folders) suggesting an older template was reused.
- Single branch (`main`), deploy-on-push to GitHub Pages.

+# Multipage Website Restructure — Lanka Global Access
+
+**Goal:** Transform the 2-page static site into a full multipage website with dedicated
+pages per section, a shared component system, and data-driven university/blog pages.
+
+## Constraints & Architecture Decisions
+
+- **Hosting:** GitHub Pages, no build system → pure HTML/CSS/JS only.
+- **Shared components:** `assets/js/components.js` injects header (with dropdown nav),
+  footer, and WhatsApp button into every page. Single point of maintenance for nav/contact info.
+- **Design system:** extracted from current inline styles into `assets/css/site.css`
+  (tokens: `--primary #1e40af`, accent amber, Poppins + Playfair Display).
+- **Shared behavior:** `assets/js/site.js` (loader, scrolled header, mobile menu,
+  AOS/GSAP init, reveal animations).
+- **Data-driven pages:** universities and blog posts live in plain-JS data files
+  (`assets/js/data/*.js`) rendered by one template page each via `?id=` query param —
+  avoids hand-maintaining dozens of near-identical HTML files.
+- **Path handling:** every page sets `window.SITE_ROOT` inline *before* loading
+  components.js so asset/logo/nav links resolve at any folder depth.
+- **SEO:** real HTML pages for all main sections; dynamic pages included in sitemap.xml;
+  unique title + meta description on every page.
+
+## Target URL Map
+
+```
+/                                Home
+/contact.html                    Contact Us
+
+/about/index.html                Who We Are → About Us
+/about/mission-vision.html       Mission & Vision
+/about/why-choose-us.html        Why Choose Us
+/about/testimonials.html         Testimonials
+
+/study-abroad/index.html         Study Abroad overview (country cards)
+/study-abroad/australia.html
+/study-abroad/canada.html
+/study-abroad/uk.html
+/study-abroad/new-zealand.html
+/study-abroad/usa.html
+
+/universities/index.html         Universities by country (grid)
+/universities/{australia|canada|uk|new-zealand|usa}.html   University lists
+/universities/university.html?id=<slug>                    Details + courses offered
+
+/services/student-visa.html      Student Visa Services
+/services/ielts-pte.html         IELTS/PTE Services
+
+/resources/blog.html             Blog listing
+/resources/post.html?id=<slug>   Blog post detail
+/resources/faq.html              FAQ
+```
+
+Navigation: Home · Who We Are ▾ · Study Abroad ▾ · Universities ▾ · Student Services ▾ · Resources ▾ · Contact · [Get Started]
+
+## Phases
+
+### Phase 1 — Foundation & shared components ✅ acceptance: contact.html renders fully from components
+- [ ] Folder skeleton: `about/ study-abroad/ universities/ services/ resources/ assets/{css,js/data}`
+- [ ] `assets/css/site.css` — tokens, base, header/nav/dropdowns, buttons, cards, section titles, loader, utilities
+- [ ] `assets/js/components.js` — SITE config + NAV tree; renders header, mobile menu, footer, WhatsApp float
+- [ ] `assets/js/site.js` — shared behaviors (loader hide, header scroll, mobile menu, AOS/GSAP init, counters)
+- [ ] Refactor `contact.html` to use shared components (keep its Formspree logic)
+
+### Phase 2 — Who We Are (4 pages)
+- [ ] about/index.html — story, values, stats, CTA
+- [ ] about/mission-vision.html
+- [ ] about/why-choose-us.html
+- [ ] about/testimonials.html
+
+### Phase 3 — Study Abroad (6 pages)
+- [ ] study-abroad/index.html overview
+- [ ] Country pages ×5 (requirements, costs, intake, work rights, universities teaser → cross-link)
+
+### Phase 4 — Universities
+- [ ] `assets/js/data/universities.js` (~30 universities / 5 countries with courses)
+- [ ] universities/index.html (country grid) + country pages ×5 (rendered from data)
+- [ ] university.html?id= template — profile + course table + apply CTA
+
+### Phase 5 — Student Services (2 pages)
+- [ ] services/student-visa.html — process timeline, doc checklist, sub-services
+- [ ] services/ielts-pte.html — exam comparison, prep support, class format
+
+### Phase 6 — Resources
+- [ ] `assets/js/data/blog.js` + blog.html listing + post.html?id= reader
+- [ ] resources/faq.html — categorized accordion
+
+### Phase 7 — Homepage rework & Contact polish
+- [ ] Rework index.html sections to route into new pages (About, Countries→Study Abroad,
+      Universities preview, Services, Testimonials teaser); swap in shared header/footer
+- [ ] contact.html: map/hours/info refresh consistent with new structure
+
+### Phase 8 — SEO & QA
+- [ ] Regenerate sitemap.xml (+ keep .gz updated or drop), robots.txt check
+- [ ] Internal-link audit script (all hrefs resolve), meta/title audit
+- [ ] README update
+
+## Verification
+Per phase: serve locally (`python3 -m http.server`), confirm pages load without console
+errors, links resolve. Phase 8 runs a repo-wide link/meta audit script.

Index: resources/faq.html =================================================================== --- resources/faq.html +++ resources/faq.html @@ -0,0 +1,149 @@ + + + + + + + FAQ | Lanka Global Access + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +

Frequently Asked Questions

+

Straight answers to the questions we hear every day at our Nugegoda office.

+
+ Home Resources FAQ +
+
+
+ +
+
+ + +

General

+
+
+ Is the first consultation really free? +

Yes — your first counselling session is completely free with no obligation. We only charge when you decide to proceed with a service package.

+
+
+ Where is your office and when are you open? +

19A Thalapathpitiya Road, Nugegoda. Open Monday to Sunday, 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM. Walk-ins are welcome, but booking ahead guarantees a dedicated counsellor.

+
+
+ Do you handle visit and work visas too? +

Our primary focus is student visas and study-abroad services, but we also assist with visitor visas for family members and rejection appeals across categories.

+
+
+ + +

Study Abroad

+
+
+ Which country is cheapest for Sri Lankan students? +

Canada (public colleges) and regional Australia/NZ typically offer the best total cost. Germany is nearly tuition-free but has different entry requirements — ask us about it in counselling.

+
+
+ Can I study abroad after O/Ls? +

Yes — foundation programs in the UK, Australia and NZ accept post-O/L students, creating a bridge into bachelor's degrees. A/L students can enter diplomas or direct year-one entry.

+
+
+ Are scholarships available for Sri Lankans? +

Many partner universities offer automatic merit scholarships of 10–30% based on A/L or degree results. Graduate assistantships exist in the US and Canada. We shortlist what you qualify for.

+
+
+ How early should I start preparing? +

Ideally 8–12 months before your target intake: 1–2 months for tests, 2–3 months for applications and offers, then 2–3 months for visa processing and financials.

+
+
+ + +

Visas

+
+
+ My visa was rejected before. Can LGA help? +

Yes — rejections usually stem from fixable documentation or credibility issues. We review the refusal letter line-by-line, rebuild the file and manage appeals or fresh applications.

+
+
+ Can my spouse or children come with me? +

Depends on destination and level: Australian master's students can bring dependants with work rights; Canada allows spouses of eligible college/university students; UK now restricts dependants to research programmes. We assess per case.

+
+
+ What if my visa is refused even with LGA's help? +

We analyse the refusal grounds free of charge and advise honestly whether an appeal or re-application has merit — including cases where waiting a cycle improves odds.

+
+
+ + +

IELTS & PTE

+
+
+ Which test is easier — IELTS or PTE? +

Neither is universally easier — fit decides. Computer-comfortable students often prefer PTE's AI scoring; strong conversational speakers may prefer IELTS. Take our free diagnostic to see yours.

+
+
+ How long does preparation take? +

Most students reach target scores in 4–8 weeks with structured training. Re-attempts chasing a single band often need just 2–3 weeks of focused coaching.

+
+
+ Are classes available online? +

Yes — live-streamed classes mirror our Nugegoda batches, including speaking labs and graded mock exams with feedback.

+
+
+ + +

Process & Payments

+
+
+ When do I pay university tuition — to LGA or the university? +

Always directly to the university through official channels — we never hold your tuition money. We guide the transfer and provide receipt documentation for your visa file.

+
+
+ What are LGA's service charges? +

Charges vary by package and destination and are quoted transparently in writing before you commit. Many university applications are free under our partner agreements.

+
+
+ Do you help with accommodation and flights? +

Yes — pre-departure support includes accommodation guidance (university halls vs shared housing), ticketing advice, insurance and arrival briefings.

+
+
+
+
+ + +
+
+

Still Have Questions?

+

Ask us directly — WhatsApp, phone or a walk-in chat at our Nugegoda office.

+ Contact Us +
+

modified this website in to a multipage  website with this structure....Multipage Website Structure
Who we are? -> About US,Mission and Vision,Why Choose Us,Our Testimonials ((each section have dedicated   pages))
Study Abroad - > Study in Australia,Study in Canada,Study in UK,Study in New zealand,Study in USA (each section have dedicated   pages)
Universities - >Country -> universities- ( when customer go to  university page they can see the details about university and courses there are offering)
Student Services - >Student  Visa Services,IELTS/PTE Services, (each section have dedicated   pages)
Resources - Blog,FAQ (each section have dedicated   pages)
Contact Us ...create a plan to restructure the webpage and the codebase and add new components..write the plan to .opencode/plans directory and start implementing phase by phase systematically

The user wants to restructure the website into a multipage website with this structure:

1. **Who we are?** → About Us, Mission and Vision, Why Choose Us, Our Testimonials (each with dedicated pages)
2. **Study Abroad** → Study in Australia, Study in Canada, Study in UK, Study in New Zealand, Study in USA (each with dedicated pages)
3. **Universities** → Country → universities (university page shows details about university and courses offered)
4. **Student Services** → Student Visa Services, IELTS/PTE Services (each with dedicated pages)
5. **Resources** → Blog, FAQ (each with dedicated pages)
6. **Contact Us**

They want:
- A plan written to `.opencode/plans` directory
- Then implement phase by phase systematically

Let me create a comprehensive plan first. This is a big task. Let me think about the architecture:

**Current state:**
- Static site, GitHub Pages at www.lgavisa.com
- index.html + contact.html
- Tailwind CDN, GSAP, AOS, Font Awesome via CDN
- No build system

**Target structure:**
```
/
├── index.html                      # Home
├── contact.html                    # Contact Us
├── about/
│   ├── about-us.html              (or index.html per folder)
│   ├── mission-vision.html
│   ├── why-choose-us.html
│   └── testimonials.html
├── study-abroad/
│   ├── australia.html
│   ├── canada.html
│   ├── uk.html
│   ├── new-zealand.html
│   └── usa.html
├── universities/
│   ├── index.html                 # Country listing
│   ├── country.html?country=australia ... or
│   ├── australia.html             # universities in Australia
│   ├── canada.html
│   ├── uk.html
│   ├── new-zealand.html
│   ├── usa.html
│   └── university template page: university.html?slug=xxx OR individual pages
├── services/
│   ├── student-visa.html
│   └── ielts-pte.html
├── resources/
│   ├── blog.html (or blog/index.html)
│   └── faq.html
```

Since it's GitHub Pages static hosting without a build system, query params (?slug=) work but aren't SEO-friendly for sitemap. For a consultancy site, having real HTML files per university is better for SEO but could be many files. A pragmatic approach:

- Universities section: `/universities/index.html` lists countries; each country page `/universities/australia.html` etc. lists universities; each university gets its own page like `/universities/australia/university-of-melbourne.html`. That's a LOT of pages if there are many universities.

Alternative pragmatic approach used often: one `university-details.html` page driven by JS from a shared `universities-data.js` file, using query string `?id=university-slug`. For SEO they can add these URLs to sitemap.xml. Given no build system, this is the most maintainable approach — data lives in one JS file, easy to add/edit universities and courses.

I'll propose that hybrid:
- Real pages for all main sections (SEO-friendly)
- Data-driven dynamic rendering for universities (single template + JS data file), since course/university data changes frequently

Also shared components problem: header/footer/nav repeated across ~18+ pages. Without a build system, options:
1. Duplicate header/footer in every page (current approach, painful to maintain)
2. JS-injected partials (components.js that injects header/footer) — common for static sites without build tools

Given the existing codebase uses inline everything, I'll propose a lightweight approach: `assets/js/components.js` that renders header/footer/nav into placeholder elements, plus `assets/js/data.js` for universities/blog data. Actually wait — the user said "add new components" — so component-based approach fits their ask.

But careful: SEO-wise JS-injected nav is acceptable-ish for Google but not ideal. For a small business site it's fine and much more maintainable. Many GitHub Pages sites do this. I'll go with it but keep critical content server-rendered... well, "server" = static HTML content in each page; only nav/footer injected via JS.

Hmm, but let me think again — duplicating header/footer across 20 pages makes future edits painful (e.g., changing phone number requires editing 20 files). The components.js approach solves that. I'll do it.

**Plan phases:**

Phase 0: Foundation
- Create folder structure
- Create shared assets: assets/css/site.css (common styles extracted from current inline styles), assets/js/main.js (shared behaviors: mobile menu, AOS init, animations, form handling), assets/js/components.js (header/footer/WhatsApp/CNAME-consistent nav)
- Update sitemap.xml, robots.txt later

Phase 1: Shared components + templates
- Header with dropdown mega-menu structure for the new nav hierarchy
- Footer
- Base template documented

Phase 2: Who We Are pages (4 pages)

Phase 3: Study Abroad pages (5 pages)

Phase 4: Universities section (index + 5 country pages + dynamic university details template + data file)

Phase 5: Student Services pages (2 pages)

Phase 6: Resources (blog list + posts data-driven?, FAQ page)

Phase 7: Contact page update, homepage update linking everything

Phase 8: SEO — sitemap.xml regeneration, robots.txt, internal links check, README update

That's a lot of implementation. Each phase should be verifiable. Let me also consider design consistency: reuse current design language (Tailwind classes, colors blue-600 etc., fonts Poppins/Playfair Display).

Content: I need to write realistic content about visa consultancy for Sri Lankan students. Use info from existing site: address 19A Thalapathpitiya Road, Nugegoda; phone +94 726338989; email admin@lgavisa.com; hours Mon-Sun 8:30 AM - 5:30 PM.

For universities data — realistic public universities in each of the 5 countries with courses. Keep it reasonable: maybe 6-10 universities per country with a few courses each.

Blog: data-driven with a few starter posts rendered client-side, plus maybe individual post pages via same query-param pattern.

FAQ: static accordion page is fine.

Let me now write the plan document to .opencode/plans/. Then start implementing phase by phase.

Plan doc name: `.opencode/plans/multipage-restructure.md`

Then implement Phase 0 + 1 first (foundation & components), then proceed. Given the size, I should be systematic. The todo tool will help track phases.

Let me look at the current index.html head/design more closely to extract the design system before building components. I've seen parts. Let me read the top of index.html (head + header markup) to replicate design language accurately.

Key things to extract:
- Fonts: Poppins (body?) + Playfair Display (font-display headings)
- Colors: primary blue (#2563eb blue-600?), gradient hero
- Loader, header scrolled state, mobile menu slide-in
- WhatsApp float button styles (class whatsapp-float defined where? style.css was deleted! Wait — whatsapp-float class was in style.css which I just deleted! And contact-card, country-image, service-card, hero-slide classes too!)

Hold on — did I break the site by deleting style.css?? Let me re-check: earlier grep showed `<link rel="stylesheet">` only for CDN links in both pages. But wait, index.html references classes like `whatsapp-float`, `hero-slide`, `service-card`, `country-image`, `contact-card`, `stat-card`, `floating-shape`, `slide-dot`... If style.css was truly never linked, those styles must be defined in an inline <style> block in index.html. Let me verify index.html has an inline <style> block containing those definitions. Earlier when I grepped `style\.css|stylesheet` I saw no local stylesheet link — good. But I must confirm the custom classes are defined inline. If not, deleting style.css broke styling!

Let me grep index.html/contact.html for e.g. `.whatsapp-float` and `.hero-slide` definitions before proceeding. Critical verification step.

Actually in my final verification I checked asset references resolve, but not CSS class definitions. Must check now.

Then build the plan. Let me get going.

Steps now:
1. Verify inline styles exist for custom classes (site integrity after previous deletion).
2. Read index.html head/header sections fully for design tokens.
3. Write plan to .opencode/plans/.
4. Implement phases with todos tracking.

# Multipage Website Restructure — Lanka Global Access

**Goal:** Transform the 2-page static site into a full multipage website with dedicated
pages per section, a shared component system, and data-driven university/blog pages.

## Constraints & Architecture Decisions

- **Hosting:** GitHub Pages, no build system → pure HTML/CSS/JS only.
- **Shared components:** `assets/js/components.js` injects header (with dropdown nav),
  footer, and WhatsApp button into every page. Single point of maintenance for nav/contact info.
- **Design system:** extracted from current inline styles into `assets/css/site.css`
  (tokens: `--primary #1e40af`, accent amber, Poppins + Playfair Display).
- **Shared behavior:** `assets/js/site.js` (loader, scrolled header, mobile menu,
  AOS/GSAP init, reveal animations).
- **Data-driven pages:** universities and blog posts live in plain-JS data files
  (`assets/js/data/*.js`) rendered by one template page each via `?id=` query param —
  avoids hand-maintaining dozens of near-identical HTML files.
- **Path handling:** every page sets `window.SITE_ROOT` inline *before* loading
  components.js so asset/logo/nav links resolve at any folder depth.
- **SEO:** real HTML pages for all main sections; dynamic pages included in sitemap.xml;
  unique title + meta description on every page.

## Target URL Map

```
/                                Home
/contact.html                    Contact Us

/about/index.html                Who We Are → About Us
/about/mission-vision.html       Mission & Vision
/about/why-choose-us.html        Why Choose Us
/about/testimonials.html         Testimonials

/study-abroad/index.html         Study Abroad overview (country cards)
/study-abroad/australia.html
/study-abroad/canada.html
/study-abroad/uk.html
/study-abroad/new-zealand.html
/study-abroad/usa.html

/universities/index.html         Universities by country (grid)
/universities/{australia|canada|uk|new-zealand|usa}.html   University lists
/universities/university.html?id=<slug>                    Details + courses offered

/services/student-visa.html      Student Visa Services
/services/ielts-pte.html         IELTS/PTE Services

/resources/blog.html             Blog listing
/resources/post.html?id=<slug>   Blog post detail
/resources/faq.html              FAQ
```

Navigation: Home · Who We Are ▾ · Study Abroad ▾ · Universities ▾ · Student Services ▾ · Resources ▾ · Contact · [Get Started]

## Phases

### Phase 1 — Foundation & shared components ✅ acceptance: contact.html renders fully from components
- [ ] Folder skeleton: `about/ study-abroad/ universities/ services/ resources/ assets/{css,js/data}`
- [ ] `assets/css/site.css` — tokens, base, header/nav/dropdowns, buttons, cards, section titles, loader, utilities
- [ ] `assets/js/components.js` — SITE config + NAV tree; renders header, mobile menu, footer, WhatsApp float
- [ ] `assets/js/site.js` — shared behaviors (loader hide, header scroll, mobile menu, AOS/GSAP init, counters)
- [ ] Refactor `contact.html` to use shared components (keep its Formspree logic)

### Phase 2 — Who We Are (4 pages)
- [ ] about/index.html — story, values, stats, CTA
- [ ] about/mission-vision.html
- [ ] about/why-choose-us.html
- [ ] about/testimonials.html

### Phase 3 — Study Abroad (6 pages)

- [ ] Country pages ×5 (requirements, costs, intake, work rights, universities teaser → cross-link)

### Phase 4 — Universities
- [ ] `assets/js/data/universities.js` (~30 universities / 5 countries with courses)
- [ ] universities/index.html (country grid) + country pages ×5 (rendered from data)
- [ ] university.html?id= template — profile + course table + apply CTA

### Phase 5 — Student Services (2 pages)
- [ ] services/student-visa.html — process timeline, doc checklist, sub-services
- [ ] services/ielts-pte.html — exam comparison, prep support, class format

### Phase 6 — Resources
- [ ] `assets/js/data/blog.js` + blog.html listing + post.html?id= reader
- [ ] resources/faq.html — categorized accordion

### Phase 7 — Homepage rework & Contact polish
- [ ] Rework index.html sections to route into new pages (About, Countries→Study Abroad,
      Universities preview, Services, Testimonials teaser); swap in shared header/footer
- [ ] contact.html: map/hours/info refresh consistent with new structure

### Phase 8 — SEO & QA
- [ ] Regenerate sitemap.xml (+ keep .gz updated or drop), robots.txt check
- [ ] Internal-link audit script (all hrefs resolve), meta/title audit
- [ ] README update

## Verification
Per phase: serve locally (`python3 -m http.server`), confirm pages load without console
errors, links resolve. Phase 8 runs a repo-wide link/meta audit script.

Now the universities pages. First `universities/index.html` (static country grid), then a country page pattern rendered from data, then the university detail template.

To avoid writing 5 nearly identical country pages, I'll make each country page thin: same HTML shell + one inline script that calls a shared renderer? But shared renderer needs to live somewhere — I could put rendering functions in components.js... cleaner: create `assets/js/university-pages.js` with `renderUniversityGrid(countryKey)` used by the 5 country pages, each page passing its key via data attribute on body or inline call.

Let me write:
1. universities/index.html — static grid of 5 country cards.
2. assets/js/university-pages.js — renders cards for a given country into #university-grid; also handles detail rendering into #university-detail for university.html (reads ?id=).
3. 5 country pages (australia, canada, uk, new-zealand, usa) — identical shells differing in title/meta/hero and the JS call.
4. universities/university.html — detail template.

university-pages.js:

```js
function renderUniversityCountryPage(countryKey) { ... builds cards into #university-grid ... }
function renderUniversityDetail() {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  const uni = lgaUniById(params.get('id'));
  if (!uni) -> show not found
  fill title/meta/description etc.
}
```

Card design: white rounded card with colored top strip per country color map, name, city+type badges, ranking line, stats row (students, fee), courses count, "View Details" button → ROOT-relative link `university.html?id=slug` from within universities folder it's just `university.html?id=`.

Colors: use Tailwind classes mapped from LGA_COUNTRIES.color: teal/red/blue/green/amber → e.g., bg-{color}-600 text-white. With CDN tailwind arbitrary class names must be complete strings present in source for JIT... The Tailwind CDN scans DOM at runtime including dynamically added nodes (it observes mutations), so dynamically generated class names work as long as full class strings appear. Since we generate e.g. 'bg-' + color + '-600' at runtime, the CDN's MutationObserver will pick up the new classes and generate CSS on the fly. That works with the Play CDN. Good.

For safety also set style background gradient inline instead of relying on dynamic classes for the strip. I'll use inline styles for colors.

University detail layout:
- breadcrumb hero with uni name
- two-col: left about paragraph + courses table; right sidebar facts (city, type, founded, ranking, students, intl fees, website link) + apply CTA + related unis (same country)
- not-found fallback

Direct eval: `var` declarations DO leak to the calling scope; `const/let` don't. So replace const with var for the test, or just use vm.runInThisContext which treats it as script → top-level const stays in that context's global? In vm.runInThisContext, `const` at top level of the script is scoped to that script only too.

Here are the ten questions that decide most student visa interviews — and how to answer them convincingly.', content: `

The interview stage intimidates many applicants, but it shouldn't. Officers ask a small set of predictable questions designed to test one thing: are you a genuine student? Prepare honest, specific answers to these ten and you'll walk in calm.

1. Why this university?

Name concrete reasons: course structure, faculty research, facilities, rankings — never "my agent chose it".

2. Why this course? How does it connect to your past studies?

Show a logical academic thread from your A/Ls or degree into the program you've chosen.

3. Why this country and not another?

Compare on education quality, industry exposure or research strengths — not just lifestyle.

4. Who is funding your education?

Be precise: who pays, what they earn, what documents back it up. Vague answers here sink files.

5. What will you do after graduating?

Emphasise how the qualification strengthens your career plan at home — even if you may apply for work visas later, your stated intent must be genuine study.

6. Tell me about your accommodation plans

Know the city, typical rents, and whether you'll take university housing initially.

7. What do you know about the city where you'll live?

A little research signals seriousness — transport, weather, student communities.

8. Do you have relatives abroad?

Answer truthfully. Inconsistencies discovered later are far worse than an honest "yes" now.

9. What will you do during breaks?

Mention travel or short courses — but anchor your answer to returning home for family and career.

10. Any final points?

Use this to summarise your preparation in two confident sentences.

LGA runs free mock interviews for every client we lodge. Practise these answers aloud until they sound natural — not memorised.

` }, { id: 'ielts-vs-pte-guide', title: 'IELTS vs PTE: Which English Test Should You Actually Take?', category: 'English Tests', date: '2026-06-30', readTime: '5 min', author: 'LGA Training Unit', excerpt: 'Both tests are widely accepted — but scoring style, turnaround time and your personal strengths make one clearly smarter for you. Here\'s how to choose.', content: `

Nearly every study destination accepts both IELTS and PTE Academic today. So the question isn't acceptance — it's fit.

Choose PTE when…

  • You need results fast (typically 48 hours).
  • You're comfortable speaking to a computer — AI scoring removes examiner nerves.
  • You prefer integrated tasks that combine skills (one task can score listening + writing).
  • Your destination is Australia or New Zealand, where every university accepts it.

Choose IELTS when…

  • You're targeting the UK (some routes still expect IELTS for UKVI).
  • You write well but freeze in front of screens — paper format exists.
  • You want a human examiner for speaking who can follow natural conversation.
  • Your programme lists band requirements per skill (IELTS makes these explicit).

The score conversion cheat sheet

Roughly: IELTS 6.0 ≈ PTE 50–57 · IELTS 6.5 ≈ PTE 58–64 · IELTS 7.0 ≈ PTE 65–78. Universities publish exact tables — we match them during counselling so you register for the right exam the first time.

Our advice after coaching hundreds of students: take a diagnostic of each with us before booking either. The test that matches your instincts will always produce the better result.

` }, { id: 'sop-that-wins-admissions', title: 'How to Write a Statement of Purpose That Wins Admissions', category: 'Applications', date: '2026-06-12', readTime: '7 min', author: 'LGA Counselling Team', excerpt: 'Your SOP is the only place admissions officers hear your voice. This structure has produced offers from Toronto to Melbourne for our students.', content: `

After reviewing thousands of applications, we can predict which SOPs succeed within the first paragraph. They follow a story logic, not a template feel.

The five-part structure

  1. The spark (10%) — a specific moment that started your interest. One vivid sentence beats three generic ones.
  2. The foundation (25%) — academic background and projects that prove capability. Quantify everything.
  3. The bridge (25%) — why THIS program fills a precise gap. Name modules, labs, professors.
  4. The proof beyond class (20%) — internships, volunteering, leadership that show initiative.
  5. The return (20%) — clear post-study goals connected to home-country demand. Visa officers read this section too.

Three mistakes that guarantee rejection

  • Copying templates found online — plagiarism detectors flag them instantly.
  • Listing achievements without linking them to the course.
  • Vague endings like "contribute to society". Name the industry, role and reason.

Every LGA application includes two rounds of SOP editing by counsellors who know what each university's committee looks for. Bring us your draft — or your blank page.

Here\'s exactly how it works in 2026.', content: `

If you're applying under the SDS-style stream for Canada, a GIC (Guaranteed Investment Certificate) is usually your cleanest proof of funds.

What it actually is

You deposit roughly CAD 20,635 with a participating bank (Scotiabank, ICICI, SBI Canada, CIBC and others). After landing, the bank releases it back to you in monthly instalments over 12 months — essentially a built-in living-expense budget.

Why visa officers like it

  • Funds are verified by the bank itself — no document authenticity questions.
  • It demonstrates planning, not last-minute borrowing.
  • Combined with first-year tuition payment, it often speeds processing.

How to arrange one from Sri Lanka

  1. Get your offer letter and apply to the bank online (passport + offer needed).
  2. Transfer the amount through a licensed channel — keep every receipt.
  3. Receive the Investment Balance Confirmation for your study permit file.
  4. Activate the account after arrival; funds begin releasing within weeks.

Budget note: the GIC covers living costs — you'll still show tuition payment/ability separately. Our finance team walks every Canada-bound client through the exact current amounts before lodgement.

` }, { id: 'post-study-work-rights-compared', title: 'Post-Study Work Rights Compared: Australia, Canada, UK, NZ & USA', category: 'Destinations', date: '2026-04-15', readTime: '8 min', author: 'LGA Research Desk', excerpt: 'Where you study decides how long you can stay and work after graduating. We compare the headline rules across all five major destinations.', content: `

For many families, post-study work rights tip the country decision as much as tuition. Here's the 2026 snapshot.

Australia — Temporary Graduate (subclass 485)

Bachelor graduates: ~2 years. Master's: 2–4 years depending on qualification length. Regional study adds extra years. Work limit during study: 48 hrs/fortnight.

Canada — PGWP

Up to 3 years for programs of 2+ years at eligible DLIs. Open work permit — any employer. Strong PR bridges via Express Entry CEC and PNPs.

United Kingdom — Graduate Route

Flat 2 years for bachelor's/master's completers, 3 for PhD. No job offer required, no salary threshold during the route — switch to skilled work later.

New Zealand — Post-Study Work Visa

input.content:
Frequently Asked Questions

Straight answers to the questions we hear every day at our Nugegoda office.

Home Resources FAQ

General

Is the first consultation really free?

Yes — your first counselling session is completely free with no obligation. We only charge when you decide to proceed with a service package.

Where is your office and when are you open?

19A Thalapathpitiya Road, Nugegoda. Open Monday to Sunday, 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM. Walk-ins are welcome, but booking ahead guarantees a dedicated counsellor.

Do you handle visit and work visas too?

Our primary focus is student visas and study-abroad services, but we also assist with visitor visas for family members and rejection appeals across categories.

Study Abroad

Which country is cheapest for Sri Lankan students?

Canada (public colleges) and regional Australia/NZ typically offer the best total cost. Germany is nearly tuition-free but has different entry requirements — ask us about it in counselling.

Can I study abroad after O/Ls?

Yes — foundation programs in the UK, Australia and NZ accept post-O/L students, creating a bridge into bachelor's degrees. A/L students can enter diplomas or direct year-one entry.

Are scholarships available for Sri Lankans?

Many partner universities offer automatic merit scholarships of 10–30% based on A/L or degree results. Graduate assistantships exist in the US and Canada. We shortlist what you qualify for.

How early should I start preparing?

Ideally 8–12 months before your target intake: 1–2 months for tests, 2–3 months for applications and offers, then 2–3 months for visa processing and financials.

Visas

My visa was rejected before. Can LGA help?

Yes — rejections usually stem from fixable documentation or credibility issues. We review the refusal letter line-by-line, rebuild the file and manage appeals or fresh applications.

Can my spouse or children come with me?

Depends on destination and level: Australian master's students can bring dependants with work rights; Canada allows spouses of eligible college/university students; UK now restricts dependants to research programmes. We assess per case.

What if my visa is refused even with LGA's help?

We analyse the refusal grounds free of charge and advise honestly whether an appeal or re-application has merit — including cases where waiting a cycle improves odds.

IELTS & PTE

Which test is easier — IELTS or PTE?

Neither is universally easier — fit decides. Computer-comfortable students often prefer PTE's AI scoring; strong conversational speakers may prefer IELTS. Take our free diagnostic to see yours.

How long does preparation take?

Most students reach target scores in 4–8 weeks with structured training. Re-attempts chasing a single band often need just 2–3 weeks of focused coaching.

Are classes available online?

Yes — live-streamed classes mirror our Nugegoda batches, including speaking labs and graded mock exams with feedback.

Process & Payments

When do I pay university tuition — to LGA or the university?

Always directly to the university through official channels — we never hold your tuition money. We guide the transfer and provide receipt documentation for your visa file.

What are LGA's service charges?

Charges vary by package and destination and are quoted transparently in writing before you commit. Many university applications are free under our partner agreements.

Do you help with accommodation and flights?

Yes — pre-departure support includes accommodation guidance (university halls vs shared housing), ticketing advice, insurance and arrival briefings.

Still Have Questions?

Ask us directly — WhatsApp, phone or a walk-in chat at our Nugegoda office.

Contact Us

# Lanka Global Access - Visa & Immigration Website

A professional website for Lanka Global Access Consultancy, providing visa and immigration consulting services.

## Features

- **Modern Landing Page** - Hero slideshow, services, destinations, and contact info
- **Contact Form** - Formspree integration for client inquiries
- **Responsive Design** - Works on all devices
- **Animations** - GSAP and AOS scroll animations
- **WhatsApp Integration** - Floating chat button

## File Structure

```
visa-website/
├── index.html              # Main homepage
├── contact.html            # Contact form page
├── README.md               # This file
├── CNAME                   # Custom domain (www.lgavisa.com)
├── robots.txt              # SEO robots file
├── sitemap.xml             # XML sitemap
├── sitemap.html            # HTML sitemap
└── images/                 # Website images and assets
```

## Deployment

This site is deployed on **GitHub Pages** at [www.lgavisa.com](https://www.lgavisa.com).

```bash
# Push changes to deploy
git add .
git commit -m "Update site"
git push origin main
```

## Tech Stack

- HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
- Tailwind CSS (CDN)
- GSAP + ScrollTrigger (animations)
- AOS (Animate On Scroll)
- Font Awesome (icons)
- Formspree (contact form)

## Contact

- **Email**: admin@lgavisa.com
- **Phone**: +94 726338989

input.newString:
## Features

- **Multipage Website** - About, Study Abroad, Universities, Services, Resources and Contact sections
- **Modern Landing Page** - Hero slideshow, services, study destinations, and contact info
- **University Directory** - 30+ universities across 5 countries with courses (data-driven)
- **Blog & FAQ** - Data-driven blog with detail pages and categorized FAQs
- **Contact Form** - Formspree integration for client inquiries
- **Responsive Design** - Works on all devices
- **Animations** - GSAP and AOS scroll animations
- **WhatsApp Integration** - Floating chat button
- **Shared Components** - Header/footer injected via `assets/js/components.js`

## File Structure

```
visa-website/
├── index.html                  # Homepage
├── contact.html                # Contact form page
├── about/
│   ├── index.html              # About Us
│   ├── mission-vision.html     # Mission & Vision
│   ├── why-choose-us.html      # Why Choose Us
│   └── testimonials.html       # Student Testimonials
├── study-abroad/
│   ├── index.html              # Destinations overview
│   ├── australia.html          # Australia guide
│   ├── canada.html             # Canada guide
│   ├── uk.html                 # UK guide
│   ├── new-zealand.html        # New Zealand guide
│   └── usa.html                # USA guide
├── universities/
│   ├── index.html              # Universities hub (by country)
│   ├── australia.html          # Universities in Australia
│   ├── canada.html             # Universities in Canada
│   ├── uk.html                 # Universities in the UK
│   ├── new-zealand.html        # Universities in New Zealand
│   ├── usa.html                # Universities in the USA
│   └── university.html         # University detail (?id=<slug>)
├── services/
│   ├── student-visa.html       # Student visa services
│   └── ielts-pte.html          # IELTS & PTE preparation
├── resources/
│   ├── blog.html               # Blog listing
│   ├── post.html               # Blog post detail (?id=<slug>)
│   └── faq.html                # Frequently asked questions
├── assets/
│   ├── css/site.css            # Shared design system
│   └── js/
│       ├── components.js       # Header/footer/WhatsApp injection
│       ├── site.js             # Shared behaviors (menu, AOS, GSAP)
│       ├── university-list.js  # Country university listings
│       ├── university-detail.js# University detail renderer
│       ├── blog-list.js        # Blog listing renderer
│       ├── blog-post.js        # Blog post renderer
│       └── data/
│           ├── universities.js # University + country data
│           └── blog.js         # Blog posts data
├── README.md                   # This file
├── CNAME                       # Custom domain (www.lgavisa.com)
├── robots.txt                  # SEO robots file
├── sitemap.xml                 # XML sitemap
├── sitemap.html                # HTML sitemap
└── images/                     # Website images and assets
```

### Adding content

- **Universities**: append to `LGA_UNIVERSITIES` in `assets/js/data/universities.js`; they appear automatically on country pages.
- **Blog posts**: append to `LGA_BLOG_POSTS` in `assets/js/data/blog.js`.

 A professional website for Lanka Global Access Consultancy, providing visa and immigration consulting services.
 
 ## Features
 
-- **Modern Landing Page** - Hero slideshow, services, destinations, and contact info
+- **Multipage Website** - About, Study Abroad, Universities, Services, Resources and Contact sections
+- **Modern Landing Page** - Hero slideshow, services, study destinations, and contact info
+- **University Directory** - 30+ universities across 5 countries with courses (data-driven)
+- **Blog & FAQ** - Data-driven blog with detail pages and categorized FAQs
 - **Contact Form** - Formspree integration for client inquiries
 - **Responsive Design** - Works on all devices
 - **Animations** - GSAP and AOS scroll animations
 - **WhatsApp Integration** - Floating chat button
+- **Shared Components** - Header/footer injected via `assets/js/components.js`
 
 ## File Structure
 
 ```
 visa-website/
-├── index.html              # Main homepage
-├── contact.html            # Contact form page
-├── README.md               # This file
-├── CNAME                   # Custom domain (www.lgavisa.com)
-├── robots.txt              # SEO robots file
-├── sitemap.xml             # XML sitemap
-├── sitemap.html            # HTML sitemap
-└── images/                 # Website images and assets
+├── index.html                  # Homepage
+├── contact.html                # Contact form page
+├── about/
+│   ├── index.html              # About Us
+│   ├── mission-vision.html     # Mission & Vision
+│   ├── why-choose-us.html      # Why Choose Us
+│   └── testimonials.html       # Student Testimonials
+├── study-abroad/
+│   ├── index.html              # Destinations overview
+│   ├── australia.html          # Australia guide
+│   ├── canada.html             # Canada guide
+│   ├── uk.html                 # UK guide
+│   ├── new-zealand.html        # New Zealand guide
+│   └── usa.html                # USA guide
+├── universities/
+│   ├── index.html              # Universities hub (by country)
+│   ├── australia.html          # Universities in Australia
+│   ├── canada.html             # Universities in Canada
+│   ├── uk.html                 # Universities in the UK
+│   ├── new-zealand.html        # Universities in New Zealand
+│   ├── usa.html                # Universities in the USA
+│   └── university.html         # University detail (?id=<slug>)
+├── services/
+│   ├── student-visa.html       # Student visa services
+│   └── ielts-pte.html          # IELTS & PTE preparation
+├── resources/
+│   ├── blog.html               # Blog listing
+│   ├── post.html               # Blog post detail (?id=<slug>)
+│   └── faq.html                # Frequently asked questions
+├── assets/
+│   ├── css/site.css            # Shared design system
+│   └── js/
+│       ├── components.js       # Header/footer/WhatsApp injection
+│       ├── site.js             # Shared behaviors (menu, AOS, GSAP)
+│       ├── university-list.js  # Country university listings
+│       ├── university-detail.js# University detail renderer
+│       ├── blog-list.js        # Blog listing renderer
+│       ├── blog-post.js        # Blog post renderer
+│       └── data/

+├── sitemap.html                # HTML sitemap
+└── images/                     # Website images and assets
 ```
 
+### Adding content
+
+- **Universities**: append to `LGA_UNIVERSITIES` in `assets/js/data/universities.js`; they appear automatically on country pages.
+- **Blog posts**: append to `LGA_BLOG_POSTS` in `assets/js/data/blog.js`.

 This site is deployed on **GitHub Pages** at [www.lgavisa.com](https://www.lgavisa.com).
